title: Who brought the umbrella?
setting: A rainy afternoon at the office. Tanaka-san, Mai's manager, comes back soaked from lunch. While he was out, someone dropped off his umbrella, and Mai didn't catch who it was.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: modorimashita. iya, ame ni furarechaimashita yo.
lines.ja: 戻りました。いや、雨に降られちゃいましたよ。
lines.kana: もどりました。いや、あめにふられちゃいましたよ。
lines.english: I'm back. Ugh, I got caught in the rain.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: otsukaresama desu. ano, tanaka-san no kasa, koko ni arimasu yo.
lines.ja: お疲れさまです。あの、田中さんの傘、ここにありますよ。
lines.kana: おつかれさまです。あの、たなかさんのかさ、ここにありますよ。
lines.english: Welcome back. Um, your umbrella's right here.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: e? watashi no kasa wa, uchi ni aru n desu kedo.
lines.ja: え？私の傘は、うちにあるんですけど。
lines.kana: え？わたしのかさは、うちにあるんですけど。
lines.english: Huh? My umbrella's at home, though.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sakki, kore o motte kita hito ga imashita yo.
lines.ja: さっき、これを持ってきた人がいましたよ。
lines.kana: さっき、これをもってきたひとがいましたよ。
lines.english: Someone came by with it a little while ago.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: watashi ni desu ka? dare deshou.
lines.ja: 私にですか？誰でしょう。
lines.kana: わたしにですか？だれでしょう。
lines.english: For me? Who could that be?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: se ga takakute, kami ga nagai onna no hito deshita.
lines.ja: 背が高くて、髪が長い女の人でした。
lines.kana: せがたかくて、かみがながいおんなのひとでした。
lines.english: A tall woman with long hair.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jaa, tsuma kana. tsuma mo kami ga nagai n desu yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、妻かな。妻も髪が長いんですよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、つまかな。つまもかみがながいんですよ。
lines.english: Then maybe it was my wife. She's got long hair too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo, sugoku se ga takakatta desu yo.
lines.ja: でも、すごく背が高かったですよ。
lines.kana: でも、すごくせがたかかったですよ。

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jaa, tsuma ja nai desu ne. tsuma wa se ga hikui n desu.
lines.ja: じゃあ、妻じゃないですね。妻は背が低いんです。
lines.kana: じゃあ、つまじゃないですね。つまはせがひくいんです。
lines.english: Then it wasn't my wife. She's short.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ato, sutairu ga yokute, moderu mitai deshita.
lines.ja: あと、スタイルがよくて、モデルみたいでした。
lines.kana: あと、すたいるがよくて、もでるみたいでした。
lines.english: Oh, and she had a great figure. Like a model.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: moderu mitai desu ka. dare deshou ne.
lines.ja: モデルみたいですか。誰でしょうね。
lines.kana: もでるみたいですか。だれでしょうね。
lines.english: Like a model, huh. Now who could that be?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, sore kara, koe ga sugoku ookikatta desu.
lines.ja: あ、それから、声がすごく大きかったです。
lines.kana: あ、それから、こえがすごくおおきかったです。
lines.english: Oh, and her voice was really loud.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: koe ga ookii hito desu ka? aa, sore wa musume desu yo!
lines.ja: 声が大きい人ですか？ああ、それは娘ですよ！
lines.kana: こえがおおきいひとですか？ああ、それはむすめですよ！
lines.english: A loud voice? Oh, that was my daughter!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: hai. tsuma mo watashi mo se ga hikui noni, musume wa se ga takai n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。妻も私も背が低いのに、娘は背が高いんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。つまもわたしもせがひくいのに、むすめはせがたかいんですよ。
lines.english: Yes. My wife and I are both short, and yet our daughter's tall.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: musume-san, hontou ni sutairu ga yokatta desu yo.
lines.ja: 娘さん、ほんとうにスタイルがよかったですよ。
lines.kana: むすめさん、ほんとうにすたいるがよかったですよ。
lines.english: Your daughter really did have a lovely figure.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. uchi de mo koe ga ookii n desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。うちでも声が大きいんですけどね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。うちでもこえがおおきいんですけどね。
lines.english: Thank you. She's loud at home too, mind you.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kaeri wa, kasa o sasemasu ne.
lines.ja: 帰りは、傘をさせますね。
lines.kana: かえりは、かさをさせますね。
lines.english: Well, at least you'll have an umbrella to put up on the way home.

choices.english: His daughter dropped off his umbrella, and he worked out who she was from Mai's description.
His wife dropped off his umbrella while he was out, and Mai recognised her at once.
A tall woman came to borrow his umbrella, and Mai couldn't say who she was.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Tanaka-san got caught in the rain (ame ni furarechaimashita). Lines 2-4: Mai says someone brought his umbrella in while he was out. Lines 6-12: she describes the visitor: tall, long hair, a great figure, a loud voice. In line 7 he guesses his wife, but in line 9 he rules her out because his wife is short. In line 13 the loud voice tells him who it was: his daughter (musume). B is wrong: Tanaka-san only guessed his wife (line 7), and the visitor was too tall to be her (line 9). Mai didn't know who it was. C is wrong: nobody borrowed anything. The woman brought his umbrella from home (lines 3-4).

questions.english: You're at a company party with Mai. Tanaka-san's daughter is over there, taller than everyone around her, and Mai asks you which one she is. Point her out using se ga takai.
questions.ja: 田中さんの娘さんって、どの人？
questions.kana: たなかさんのむすめさんって、どのひと？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no musume-san tte, dono hito?
questions.answer: Point out the tall one: ano se ga takai hito (that tall person). Before a noun, ga often becomes no: se no takai hito.

modelAnswers.romaji: asoko no, se ga takai hito da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あそこの、背が高い人だよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: ano se no takai hito desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あの背の高い人ですよ。

questions.explanation: Mai describes the visitor with se ga takai in lines 6 and 8 (se ga takakute, se ga takakatta), and Tanaka-san uses it for his daughter in line 15 (musume wa se ga takai n desu). Takai on its own is for things (high, expensive), so ano hito wa takai doesn't mean that person is tall. For a person's height you need se ga takai. In front of a noun it's se ga takai hito or, more often, se no takai hito. In casual speech ga often drops: se takai ne.

questions.english: Tanaka-san is sure the visitor wasn't his wife. What did he say about his wife?
questions.ja: 田中さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: My wife's short. (with mijikai, 'short in length')
choices.romaji: tsuma wa se ga mijikai n desu.

choices.english: My wife is low. (hikui with no se)

choices.romaji: tsuma wa se ga hikui n desu.

questions.explanation: Line 9: tsuma wa se ga hikui n desu. Mai has just said the visitor was really tall, so it can't have been his wife. In Japanese, height is high or low, so short is hikui. A is the English word 'short' carried over: mijikai is for length and time (hair, a film), never height. B drops se: hikui on its own describes things (a low ceiling, low heels). For a person's height you need se ga hikui. He uses it again in line 15: tsuma mo watashi mo se ga hikui noni (my wife and I are both short, and yet...).

questions.english: Mai remembers one more thing about the visitor: koe ga sugoku ookikatta. What does she mean?

choices.english: She had a very high-pitched voice.
She talked a lot and kept chatting.

questions.explanation: Line 12: for a voice, ookii (big) means loud, so koe ga ookii is a loud voice. A would be koe ga takai, which means high-pitched, not loud. C is about how much someone talks, which doesn't come up in the scene. The loud voice is what tells Tanaka-san it was his daughter (line 13), and in line 17 he adds that she's loud at home too (uchi de mo koe ga ookii n desu kedo ne).

questions.english: Someone dropped off a parcel for Tanaka-san while he was out. You didn't get her name, but she had long hair. He asks who it was. Answer using kami ga nagai.
questions.answer: Say you don't know, but it was someone with long hair: kami ga nagai hito deshita. To add a second detail, change nagai to nagakute: kami ga nagakute, se ga takai hito deshita.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakarimasen kedo, kami ga nagai hito deshita.
modelAnswers.ja: わかりませんけど、髪が長い人でした。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not sure, but it was someone with long hair.

modelAnswers.romaji: kami ga nagakute, se ga takai hito deshita yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 髪が長くて、背が高い人でしたよ。
modelAnswers.english: It was someone tall, with long hair.

questions.explanation: In line 6 Mai answers Tanaka-san's 'dare deshou' the same way: se ga takakute, kami ga nagai onna no hito deshita. Japanese doesn't 'have' hair, so don't say nagai kami o motte imashita. The hair is the subject: kami ga nagai, as in line 7 (tsuma mo kami ga nagai n desu yo). To join two descriptions, change -i to -kute, as Mai does with takai in line 6: takakute.

questions.english: Tanaka-san shows you a photo of his daughter on his phone. She's tall and slim. Compliment her figure using sutairu ga ii.
questions.kana: これが、うちのむすめです。
questions.romaji: kore ga, uchi no musume desu.
questions.answer: Compliment her figure: sutairu ga ii desu ne! You can add moderu mitai desu (like a model), as Mai does.

modelAnswers.romaji: sutairu ga ii desu ne! moderu mitai desu.
modelAnswers.ja: スタイルがいいですね！モデルみたいです。
modelAnswers.english: She has a lovely figure! Just like a model.

modelAnswers.romaji: se ga takakute, sutairu ga ii desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 背が高くて、スタイルがいいですね。
modelAnswers.english: She's tall and has a great figure, doesn't she?

questions.explanation: Mai uses it twice: sutairu ga yokute, moderu mitai deshita (line 10) and musume-san, hontou ni sutairu ga yokatta desu yo (line 16). Ii changes to yoku- when it inflects: yokute, yokatta. Sutairu ga ii is a compliment on someone's body (slim, well-proportioned), not their clothes. To praise her clothes, say oshare desu ne. Speaking to your manager, keep it polite with desu ne. With a friend it's just sutairu ii ne!

newWords.english: a little while ago, just now
(fashion) model; moderu mitai = like a model
